view.stem: 图中两条平行直线被另一条直线截交。选出所有对应边的方向分别相同的角对；仅大小相等并不表示对应边同向。

options.text: $\angle APN$ 与 $\angle CQN$
$\angle NPB$ 与 $\angle NQD$
$\angle BPM$ 与 $\angle DQM$
$\angle MPA$ 与 $\angle MQC$
$\angle APN$ 与 $\angle DQM$
$\angle NPB$ 与 $\angle MQC$
$\angle APN$ 与 $\angle CQM$
$\angle BPM$ 与 $\angle DQN$

intent.task: Identify all four sector correspondences having the same directions on both corresponding sides, rather than all equal-measure pairs.
intent.source_solution: In the actual figure A-P-B and C-Q-D are horizontal and M-Q-P-N is the rising transversal. PA/QC point left, PB/QD right, PN/QN up-right, PM/QM down-left. The complete same-direction pairs are APN/CQN, NPB/NQD, BPM/DQM and MPA/MQC. Reversing both rays can preserve the measure but does not satisfy the requested direction criterion. Equivalent names using Q on PM or P on QN add no new sector.
intent.unit_reason: One multiple-response collection judges all four sectors against one definition. Splitting into yes/no clicks would repeat the same operation and obscure completeness.
limitations: Recognizing the complete collection does not demonstrate independently enumerating and writing all corresponding angle pairs.

figure_observations.observation: Opened the complete actual SVG once: A-P-B above C-Q-D, transversal M-Q-P-N rising to the right; N, M and the rightmost D were visible. The visible modern glyphs are used as written; historical alphabet provenance is UNKNOWN.

rationales.derivation: PA and QC both point left; PN and QN both point up-right. These are the two side correspondences.
PN/QN point up-right and PB/QD point right, so both corresponding directions agree.
PB/QD point right and PM/QM down-left, so both corresponding directions agree.
PM/QM point down-left and PA/QC left, so both corresponding directions agree.
PA is left while QD is right; PN is up-right while QM is down-left. Both pairs are opposite, not same.
rationales.misconception: Reverse both rays of APN to obtain the congruent DQM sector, then incorrectly infer same directions from equality of angle measures.

rationales.derivation: PN is up-right while QM is down-left; PB is right while QC is left. Both correspondences reverse direction.
rationales.misconception: Select the congruent opposite-facing acute sector MQC for NPB, substituting equal size for the required same-direction correspondence.

rationales.derivation: PA/QC agree but PN/QM are opposite. Keeping the horizontal side does not fix the reversed transversal side.
rationales.misconception: Match the left-pointing sides PA and QC, then take QM instead of QN simply because both lie on the transversal's line.

rationales.derivation: PB/QD agree but PM/QN are opposite, so only one correspondence has the same direction.
rationales.misconception: Match the right-pointing sides PB and QD, then disregard the ray direction on the transversal and replace down-left QM by up-right QN.

view.stem:
已知角 $AOB$，要作一个顶点为已知点 $M$ 的角，使对应边分别都同向，或分别都反向。位置条件写为：

1) $M$ 在角 $AOB$ 的一条边上；
2) $M$ 不在角 $AOB$ 的一条边上。

哪一套步骤在这两种表述的情形下都能完成同向与反向两种作法？

options.text: 将整个角按把 $A$ 移到 $M$ 的平移移动，取两条像射线；再把两条像射线都反向，作为另一种作法。
将整个角按把 $O$ 移到 $M$ 的平移移动，取两条像射线；再仅把 $OB$ 的像射线反向，作为另一种作法。
将整个角按把 $O$ 移到 $M$ 的平移移动，取两条像射线；再把两条像射线都反向，作为另一种作法。
从 $M$ 分别经过 $A$、$B$ 作射线 $MA$、$MB$，取这两条射线；再把它们都反向，作为另一种作法。

intent.task: Recognize a complete construction for both same-direction and opposite-direction corresponding rays, for both literal positional clauses about M.
intent.source_solution: Translate both original rays together by O to M. The images start at M and preserve the directions of OA and OB. Reverse both image rays for the opposite-direction construction, equivalently apply a half-turn at M. If M is on a side, use its existing supporting line with the required direction; no distinct parallel line is needed. If M is off a side, take the parallel direction through M. This works even for M=O. The wording 'M 不在角 AOB 的一条边上' is ambiguous between failure to lie on a specified side and an off-both-sides reading; do not silently equate those readings. The construction works for any M under either reading without resolving that classification.
intent.unit_reason: A single complete procedure covers both position statements and both orientation requests. The point's location does not change the direction-transport operation.
limitations: Recognition does not demonstrate drawing either construction, making parallels, or physically choosing the correct half-rays when M is on a supporting line.
The literal second position clause remains ambiguous; successful invariant construction does not determine its intended reading or make the two clauses disjoint.

rationales.derivation: A-to-M translation moves the vertex to O+(M-A), which generally differs from M because O differs from A. Reversing rays does not move this wrong vertex.
rationales.misconception: Treat the named side point A as the angle's vertex, choose the translation by A to M, and keep the image rays at the resulting wrong origin.

rationales.derivation: The first construction is valid, but the second keeps OA's direction and reverses only OB's direction. It is mixed, not both opposite.
rationales.misconception: Transport the angle correctly, then identify 'opposite angle' with reversing just one ray instead of both corresponding rays.

rationales.derivation: The O-to-M translation gives two rays with origin M and the original respective directions. Reversing each ray at M produces the two respective opposite directions. Both steps are valid regardless of the literal clause-2 reading.
For a general M, MA and MB need not be parallel to OA and OB. If M lies beyond A on OA, MA is even opposite to OA; if M=A it fails to specify a ray. Reversing both does not fix the general mismatch.
rationales.misconception: Replace changing the origin while preserving a direction by joining the new origin to each old endpoint; then reverse those endpoint-joining rays as if they were transported directions.

view.stem: 点 $B$ 在点 $A$ 和 $C$ 之间。下表哪一行依次给出 $[AB)$ 与 $[BC)$、$[AB)$ 与 $[CB)$ 两方向之间的夹角？

intent.task: Determine the complete ordered pair of directional angles for collinear points A-B-C, contrasting same and opposite directions.
intent.source_solution: The order A-B-C makes AB and BC point from the A end toward the C end, hence 0 degrees. CB points from C back toward A, opposite to AB, hence 180 degrees. Origins and segment lengths are irrelevant to the angle between directions.
intent.unit_reason: The two entries form one coherent direction-reversal comparison. A complete row preserves their relationship without isolated answer-cell clicks.
limitations: Selection does not demonstrate writing both results independently or drawing the collinear rays and transporting their origins.

rationales.derivation: AB and BC have different origins but identical direction, so the first 180-degree entry is wrong; AB and CB are opposite, so the second is right.
rationales.misconception: Use different origins as a rule for opposition on a common line, assigning 180 degrees to both pairs instead of tracking the named ray directions.

rationales.derivation: A-to-B and B-to-C point along the same direction, giving 0; C-to-B reverses that direction, giving 180 against A-to-B.
The first 0 is right, but CB reverses AB and requires 180, not 0.
rationales.misconception: Discard the endpoint order and treat every ray on the same supporting line as the same direction, assigning 0 to both pairs.

rationales.derivation: Both entries are swapped relative to the actual ray directions: BC is not opposite AB, and CB is not same as AB.
rationales.misconception: Keep AB as A-to-B but read each second ray backward: read BC as C-to-B and CB as B-to-C, obtaining 180 then 0.

view.stem: 作出射线 $AB$ 和 $CD$ 后，要在已知点 $M$ 作一个角，其大小等于这两条射线方向之间的夹角。$A$ 与 $C$ 不要求重合。哪一套步骤对所作的射线都适用？

options.text: 把两条射线一起按 $A$ 移到 $M$ 的平移移动；取两条像射线之间的凸角，同向时记作 $0^\circ$。
分别按 $A$ 移到 $M$、$C$ 移到 $M$ 平移两条射线；只将 $CD$ 的像反向，再取所得射线的凸角。
分别按 $A$ 移到 $M$、$C$ 移到 $M$ 平移两条射线；取凸角另一侧的角，大小为 $360^\circ$ 减去凸角。
分别按 $A$ 移到 $M$、$C$ 移到 $M$ 平移两条射线；取两条像射线之间的凸角，同向时记作 $0^\circ$。

intent.task: Recognize the complete construction transporting two independently based rays to a common specified vertex, with the defined directional-angle sector.
intent.source_solution: Draw AB and CD, then translate AB by A to M and CD separately by C to M. Both image origins are M and both respective directions are preserved. Their convex angle is the original direction angle, with identical directions giving 0 and opposite directions giving 180. One common translation cannot identify distinct origins A and C. Reversing one image ray gives the supplement; the other sector gives the reflex angle rather than the defined directional value.
intent.unit_reason: The essential operation is the complete pair of origin transports plus selection of the defined sector. It is different from moving a whole angle with one common original vertex.
limitations: Text recognition does not demonstrate drawing the initial rays, constructing the two parallels through M, or producing the final angle and its sector.

rationales.derivation: Under A-to-M translation, AB starts at M but CD starts at C+(M-A). For A different from C this is not M, so the two rays do not construct the requested vertex.
rationales.misconception: Reuse a single translation for two distinct original origins, forgetting that a translation preserves their displacement and cannot send both to M.

rationales.derivation: The origins are correct, but reversing only CD's direction changes a general directional angle t to 180-t. These agree only in the special right-angle case, not for all rays.
rationales.misconception: Treat replacing a ray by the opposite ray as preserving its direction angle, effectively using an unoriented supporting line for CD.

rationales.derivation: For a convex directional value t, this procedure selects 360-t instead of t. It does not give the quantity defined in the selected lesson, including the 0-degree convention.
rationales.misconception: After correctly joining the origins, choose the outside/reflex sector and measure a full revolution minus the requested convex sector.

rationales.derivation: Each original starting point is independently sent to M, preserving its ray's direction. The common-origin convex angle is precisely the definition of the angle between those directions.

view.stem: 两个凸角 $AOB$、$CVD$ 的对应边分别反向：$OA$ 与 $VC$ 反向，$OB$ 与 $VD$ 反向。哪段推理能证明这两个角全等？

options.text: 将第一角平移，使 $O$ 到达 $V$，再绕 $V$ 旋转 $180^\circ$。两条像射线分别与 $VC$、$VD$ 重合；两次变换保角，所以全等。
将第一角平移，使 $O$ 到达 $V$，不再旋转。两条像射线分别与 $VC$、$VD$ 重合；平移保角，所以两角全等。
将第一角平移，使 $O$ 到达 $V$，再绕 $V$ 旋转 $90^\circ$。两条像射线分别与 $VC$、$VD$ 重合；两次变换保角，所以全等。
将第一角平移，使 $O$ 到达 $V$，旋转 $180^\circ$ 后仅将第二条像射线反向。两条射线分别与 $VC$、$VD$ 重合，所以两角全等。

intent.task: Recognize a complete congruence proof for two convex angles with both corresponding ray directions reversed.
intent.source_solution: Translate the first vertex O to V. A half-turn about V reverses each translated ray, making them coincide with VC and VD respectively. Both transformations preserve the convex angle, proving congruence. Translation alone preserves rather than reverses directions; a quarter-turn makes perpendicular directions; reversing just one ray after the half-turn destroys one of the required coincidences.
intent.unit_reason: A single entire transformation chain preserves the proof's decisive two-ray mapping and angle-preservation argument, rather than asking for just a theorem name or final equality.
limitations: Selecting a complete proof does not demonstrate inventing, drawing, or independently writing the translation and half-turn argument.

rationales.derivation: After O-to-V translation, a half-turn sends the two preserved original directions to their two given opposite directions. Both rays and the vertex match, and angle measure is preserved.
Translation leaves each image ray opposite to its corresponding target ray, so the asserted coincidence is false. The true target theorem is not established by this claimed mapping.
rationales.misconception: Align the vertices and treat lying on the same supporting line as coincidence of rays, ignoring that both directions remain reversed.

rationales.derivation: A 90-degree rotation makes each image ray perpendicular to its original direction, not opposite to it. It cannot coincide with the given opposite target direction.
rationales.misconception: Substitute a quarter-turn for a half-turn when turning a ray to its opposite direction, then incorrectly claim both target rays coincide.

rationales.derivation: The half-turn initially makes both targets coincide. Reversing the second ray again makes it opposite to VD, so the final two-ray coincidence assertion is false.
rationales.misconception: Apply a correct half-turn, then reverse the second side once more as an extra 'opposite-side' step, undoing only that side's match.

view.stem: 两个凸角的大小为 $x$、$y$。一对对应边同向，另一对对应边反向。哪段推理能证明 $x+y=180^\circ$？

options.text: 平移一个角，使同向的两条边重合。另两条边在同一直线上，因此也重合；两角相等，故 $x=y=90^\circ$。
平移一个角使顶点重合，再把整个角转 $90^\circ$。两角都变成直角，因此各为 $90^\circ$，总和为 $180^\circ$。
平移一个角，使同向的两条边重合。另两条边是相反射线，两凸角是邻角并组成平角，因此 $x+y=180^\circ$。
平移一个角，使同向的两条边重合。另两条边是相反射线，两角围成整个周角，因此 $x+y=360^\circ$。

intent.task: Recognize the complete supplementation proof for one same-direction and one opposite-direction corresponding side pair.
intent.source_solution: Translate to the common vertex so the same-direction rays coincide. The remaining rays are opposite and form a straight line. The two convex angles are adjacent sectors partitioning a straight angle, so x+y=180. They need not be equal or individually right angles, and they do not cover a full revolution.
intent.unit_reason: The proof's unit is the entire common-ray and opposite-rays argument, not an isolated sum cell. Its mixed direction premise and adjacent sectors differ from the both-opposite congruence proof.
limitations: Recognition cannot establish independently drawing the auxiliary common-vertex arrangement or producing the adjacent-angle proof.

rationales.derivation: The remaining rays share a line but point oppositely, so they do not coincide. The premise permits unequal supplementary values; it does not force two 90-degree angles.
rationales.misconception: Replace two opposite rays by one unoriented line, declare both angles identical, then combine that false equality with the desired 180 sum to assign 90 to each.

rationales.derivation: Rotating an entire angle by 90 degrees preserves its internal measure; it does not make that measure 90. The step forcing both angles to be right is false.
rationales.misconception: Confuse the rotation of the whole figure by 90 degrees with setting the separation of its own two rays to 90 degrees, then add two purported right angles.

rationales.derivation: Same-direction rays coincide after translation. The other two rays remain opposite, so the two convex sectors are adjacent and exactly partition the straight 180-degree sector.
The opposite remaining rays span a straight angle on the side containing the common ray. The selected adjacent convex sectors cover 180, not the entire 360-degree revolution.
rationales.misconception: Correctly identify opposite bounding rays but treat the two adjacent convex sectors as a complete revolution rather than a half-plane, doubling their total.

view.stem: 按两方向之间的夹角取凸角大小。哪一行完整给出南方与西方、南方与北方、东方与东南方的夹角？

options.text:
| 南方与西方 | 南方与北方 | 东方与东南方 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $270^\circ$ | $180^\circ$ | $315^\circ$ |

| 南方与西方 | 南方与北方 | 东方与东南方 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $90^\circ$ | $180^\circ$ | $45^\circ$ |

| 南方与西方 | 南方与北方 | 东方与东南方 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $90^\circ$ | $0^\circ$ | $45^\circ$ |

| 南方与西方 | 南方与北方 | 东方与东南方 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $90^\circ$ | $180^\circ$ | $90^\circ$ |

intent.task: Determine all three compass-direction angles, distinguishing adjacent cardinal directions, opposite directions, and a half-quadrant.
intent.source_solution: South and west differ by a quarter-turn, giving 90 degrees. South and north are opposite, giving 180. Southeast is halfway between east and south, so east and southeast give 45. Use the convex-direction-angle definition, not the reflex travel route.
intent.unit_reason: One complete table row retains the whole three-part compass comparison; no separate arithmetic cell or incidental direction-word copying is asked.
limitations: Selection does not demonstrate independently calculating and writing the three values or constructing a compass rose.

rationales.derivation: These entries are the full-revolution complements of the correct convex values: 360-90=270, 360-180=180 and 360-45=315. The definition does not select those reflex values.
rationales.misconception: Compute the shorter separations, then systematically replace each by the other route around the compass, using 360 degrees minus each value.

rationales.derivation: Adjacent cardinal south/west give 90; opposite south/north give 180; east/southeast is half of the east/south 90-degree quadrant, giving 45.
The first and third values are right, but south and north are opposite ray directions, requiring 180 rather than 0.
rationales.misconception: Collapse the north-south axis to an unoriented supporting line and identify its two opposite compass directions, while calculating the other two separations normally.

rationales.derivation: The two cardinal comparisons are right, but east/southeast is half a quadrant, not a whole 90-degree quadrant.
rationales.misconception: Replace southeast by south when counting compass quadrants, so east-to-southeast is mistakenly counted as the entire east-to-south quarter-turn.

view.stem: 图中 $(AC)\parallel(FE)$，$\alpha$ 已标在 $\angle CBD$ 内。除这个已标出的角外，选出在交点 $B$、$D$ 处所有大小等于 $\alpha$ 的凸角。

options.text: $\angle ABR$
$\angle CBR$
$\angle ABD$
$\angle EDP$
$\angle EDR$
$\angle FDR$
$\angle FDP$

intent.task: Identify the complete set of alpha-equal sectors at both intersections, acknowledging the given CBD sector and assessing every other sector.
intent.source_solution: The actual descending transversal has order R-B-D-P, with A-B-C above F-D-E. CBD is the marked alpha sector. ABR reverses both of its sides, EDP keeps both directions at D, and FDR reverses both at D; all three equal alpha. CBR, ABD, EDR and FDP reverse just one of those directions and equal 180-alpha. Thus the full source collection is CBD, ABR, EDP, FDR. The pictured transversal is oblique, not perpendicular to the parallel lines; no numerical alpha is assigned.
intent.unit_reason: One multiple selection assesses all the unmarked sectors under one equality criterion. The already marked CBD is acknowledged explicitly instead of becoming an answer obtainable by copying its visible alpha label. The separate directional-angle task is handled in another complete response unit.
limitations: Selection does not demonstrate independently enumerating and writing all sectors; the marked CBD is acknowledged rather than separately tested by copying.
No numerical alpha is inferred from visual slope, and no new point or incidence is inferred from any C-adjacent speck.

figure_observations.observation: Opened the complete actual SVG once: A-B-C above F-D-E, R-B-D-P descending to the right, visible dot at D; alpha lies between rightward BC and down-right BD. C, E and bottom P were visible. Original glyph alphabet and the provenance/meaning of any C speck are UNKNOWN and supply no condition.

rationales.derivation: BA is opposite BC and BR is opposite BD. Reversing both rays of CBD gives ABR with equal measure alpha.
BC is retained but BR reverses BD. CBR is adjacent to CBD and measures 180-alpha, not alpha in the pictured oblique configuration.
rationales.misconception: Keep BC but treat BR and BD as interchangeable because they share the transversal line; reverse one ray without changing the purported angle measure.

rationales.derivation: BA reverses BC while BD stays fixed. ABD is the neighboring supplementary sector, measuring 180-alpha.
rationales.misconception: Keep BD but replace BC by opposite BA on the same horizontal line, incorrectly transporting only a supporting line instead of its ray direction.

rationales.derivation: DE has the same rightward direction as BC, and DP the same down-right direction as BD. EDP equals alpha.
DE keeps BC's direction but DR reverses BD's direction. EDR measures the supplement 180-alpha.
rationales.misconception: Move the rightward side from B to D correctly, then choose the upward ray DR instead of downward DP on the transversal, retaining the alpha label after a one-side reversal.

rationales.derivation: DF reverses BC's direction and DR reverses BD's direction. Both reversed directions preserve alpha.
DF reverses BC while DP keeps BD's direction. FDP measures 180-alpha.
rationales.misconception: Keep the downward transversal direction at D but take the leftward horizontal ray DF instead of rightward DE, ignoring the single reversed side.

view.stem: 图中 $(AC)\parallel(FE)$，$\angle CBD=\alpha$。哪一行完整给出所列四对射线方向之间的夹角？

intent.task: Determine all four direction-angle correspondences across the two vertices: identical directions, opposite directions, both reversed, and one reversed.
intent.source_solution: BC and DE point right, giving 0. BC points right and DF left, giving 180. BA points left and DR up-left: both reverse the directions of BC and BD, so their angle is alpha. BR is up-left while DE points right: only BD's direction is reversed relative to CBD, giving 180-alpha. All four values use directions rather than angles requiring the original ray origins to coincide.
intent.unit_reason: A complete four-column row preserves every source pair and the linked reversal rule. This is a common-origin direction transport task, distinct from enumerating already drawn alpha-equal sectors.
limitations: Recognition does not demonstrate independently writing the four values or drawing translated rays with a common origin.
No exact numeric alpha or additional C-speck geometry is inferred from the figure.

figure_observations.observation: Reuse of the one complete actual-SVG observation, with no reopen: A-B-C and F-D-E horizontal, order R-B-D-P on the descending transversal; alpha is CBD. Thus BC/DE are rightward, BA/DF leftward, BR/DR up-left and BD/DP down-right. Rightmost C/E and bottom P were visible; historical alphabet and C-speck provenance remain UNKNOWN.

rationales.derivation: The second entry must be 180 because BC and DF have opposite horizontal directions. The other entries match the figure.
rationales.misconception: Treat parallel horizontal supporting lines as identical directions, collapsing rightward BC and leftward DF to 0 while otherwise using the correct oblique-ray comparisons.

rationales.derivation: The last pair has BR opposite to BD while DE preserves BC, so its angle is 180-alpha rather than alpha.
rationales.misconception: Replace up-left BR by down-right BD because both are on the same transversal, so BR/DE is mistaken for the given alpha comparison.

rationales.derivation: The first pair is right/right (0), the second right/left (180), the third reverses both rays of CBD (alpha), and the fourth reverses only BD while keeping BC's direction (180-alpha).
The last two entries exchange the double-reversal and single-reversal results. BA/DR is alpha; BR/DE is 180-alpha.
rationales.misconception: Reverse the governing rule: subtract alpha from 180 when both corresponding directions are reversed, but retain alpha when just one direction is reversed.

view.stem: 两个角同为锐角，或同为钝角；它们的对应边彼此垂直。设两角大小为 $x$、$y$。哪段推理能证明这两个角全等？

options.text: 把第一角两边同向转 $90^\circ$，再移到第二角顶点。第二角两边与像角必一同向、一反向，因此 $y=180^\circ-x$；这对同为锐角和同为钝角均成立。
把第一角两边同向转 $90^\circ$，再移到第二角顶点。第二角两边与像角必都同向，因此 $y=x$；无需考虑相反射线，锐角和钝角同样成立。
先平移第一角，使它的一边与第二角对应边重合，再把两边同向转 $90^\circ$，另一边便重合。两次变换保角，所以同为锐角或同为钝角时都有 $y=x$。
把第一角两边同向转 $90^\circ$，再移到第二角顶点。对应方向或都同向、都反向，或一同一反，故 $y=x$ 或 $y=180^\circ-x$。同为锐角或同为钝角都排除后一种，因此 $y=x$。

intent.task: Recognize the complete perpendicular-side congruence proof, exhausting orientation possibilities and using both same-type cases to rule out supplementation.
intent.source_solution: Rotate the first angle's two rays in the same sense by 90 degrees and translate the vertex to the second. Each target ray is either the same as or opposite to the corresponding rotated ray, since both are perpendicular to the original ray. Both same or both opposite give y=x; one same and one opposite give y=180-x. If both angles are acute, x<90 implies 180-x>90, contradicting acute y. If both are obtuse, x>90 implies 180-x<90, contradicting obtuse y. Hence y=x in both original type cases. A mixed acute/obtuse pair is not authorized by the premise.
intent.unit_reason: One exhaustive proof chain accounts for both the rotation argument and the two angle-type exclusions. Separate acute-only examples would omit the obtuse branch and the role of the type condition.
limitations: Selecting the chain does not demonstrate independently generating or writing the rotation, complete orientation case split, and both inequality contradictions.
No extension to a mixed acute-obtuse pair or replacement by a right-angle case is claimed.

rationales.derivation: Perpendicularity allows each target direction to be either same or opposite to the rotated image; it does not require one of each. Moreover y=180-x would change an acute angle to obtuse or an obtuse angle to acute, contradicting both given same-type cases.
rationales.misconception: Assign opposite signed quarter-turns to the two corresponding rays by default, retain only the resulting supplementary case, and incorrectly treat 180-x as preserving the acute/obtuse type.

rationales.derivation: The conclusion of congruence is true but the assertion of mandatory same-direction coincidence after the fixed quarter-turn is false. The target can be opposite to both rotated rays while keeping the same measure and type.
rationales.misconception: Treat perpendicularity as specifying a unique same-sense quarter-turn. Discard the other perpendicular half-ray for each side and claim automatic coincidence instead of accounting for the both-opposite possibility.

rationales.derivation: The initial corresponding sides are perpendicular. A translation cannot make their directions coincide, so the first asserted side coincidence is impossible; the claimed two-ray mapping never follows.
rationales.misconception: Use translation to align a perpendicular ray with its target, confusing a change of position with a change of direction, then rotate as if one side were already aligned.

rationales.derivation: A same-sense quarter-turn preserves x. Perpendicularity makes each target ray same or opposite to that image. The both-same and both-opposite cases give x; a mixed case gives 180-x. For acute x that alternative is obtuse, and for obtuse x it is acute. Both stated same-type hypotheses therefore force y=x.
